content: What matters in life is not what happens to you, but what you remember and how you remember it.
author: Gabriel García Márquez
sourceWork: Gabriel García Márquez's Essays & Philosophical Writings
story:
There is a sharp, grounded clarity in this observation. Thinking about doing something gives us a comfortable dopamine hit of progress without any of the actual friction. We often use over-researching and planning as socially acceptable disguises for fear of starting.

Across his life and work, Gabriel García Márquez saw how easily we surrender our tranquility to fear, vanity, and distraction. Clarity follows action; it does not precede it. You cannot think your way into a new way of living—you have to act your way into a new way of understanding. The smallest real-world step beats the most brilliant theory.
reflectionPrompt: How can you integrate the essence of this wisdom into one specific decision or encounter today?
